mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport/national ID authority; notarization by a licensed notary public in the home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if originating state is a Convention party; otherwise Consular Legalization by the competent Canadian consulate/embassy in the originating country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address for each director, officer and individual with significant control (utility bill or bank statement dated within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or authorized deposit-taking institution; notarization by a licensed notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if originating state is a Convention party; otherwise Consular Legalization by the competent Canadian consulate/embassy in the originating country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming lawful source of funds for initial share capital and payroll / EOR escrow funding
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or securities dealer in the jurisdiction of the shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if originating state is a Convention party; otherwise Consular Legalization by the competent Canadian consulate/embassy in the originating country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized consent to act as director for each founding director, together with sworn declaration of non-bankruptcy and eligibility under OBCA
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Director signed before an Ontario notary public, commissioner for taking affidavits, or other competent foreign notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if originating state is a Convention party; otherwise Consular Legalization by the competent Canadian consulate/embassy in the originating country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate incumbency, certificate of good standing and board resolution for any non-individual or corporate shareholder/UBO in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of the foreign corporate shareholder/UBO; corporate secretary or legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if originating state is a Convention party; otherwise Consular Legalization by the competent Canadian consulate/embassy in the originating country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP, politically exposed person, and sanctions screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions Lists (SEMA/JVCFOA), United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, HM Treasury sanctions list, and applicable Canadian domestic law enforcement watchlists. Enhanced due diligence is required for foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates under FATF Recommendation 12 and FINTRAC guidance. All onboarding screening records, source-of-funds explanations and periodic re-screening outputs must be retained in the Ontario corporate AML/CFT file and made available to FINTRAC and law enforcement under applicable PCMLTFA obligations; transaction monitoring is required before any payroll distribution via local payroll direct-debit or Wise rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry (https://www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-business-registry); NUANS name search system via an authorized Ontario service provider
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names under the OBCA may be in English, French, or a combined English/French form. Non-Roman scripts and non-English/French names must be transliterated into Roman characters for the NUANS record; the legal corporate name will be the English/French transliteration appearing on the certificate. Mandatory legal identifiers (e.g., Inc., Corp., Ltd., Incorporée, Limitée) must be included in the proposed name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation in Ontario is valid for 90 days and may be renewed before expiry through the Ontario Business Registry or the NUANS service provider. If the Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request within 30 days to the Director, Companies and Personal Property Branch, attaching the original name search report, the rejection notice, and any supporting explanation or consent from a regulatory body. If the refusal is upheld, a new name application with a fresh NUANS report must be submitted; no further appeal is available except judicial review under applicable procedural law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Ontario OBCA requires a registered office at a physical street address in Ontario where corporate records and the Register of Individuals with Significant Control are kept. A simple virtual mail-forwarding service is not sufficient. A virtual office with term-rented physical premises and document-handling personnel may satisfy the registered-office requirement, but for a payroll/EOR platform, CRA and provincial employment standards authorities will expect actual management presence and payroll records in Canada. For Global EOR statutory payroll operations, a pure virtual-office arrangement is insufficient to establish commercial substance and may be challenged as a sham for payroll withholding, EI/CPP and Employment Standards Act purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% during pre-incorporation phase, rising to 35% after payroll source deductions and Ontario employer registration because CRA and the Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development may conduct compliance visits or payroll audits, especially if the EOR platform shows weak physical substance or receives employee complaints.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Ontario), RSO 1990, c B.16, ss. 2(1), 8, 9, 20, 95, 115, 123, 126; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 (optional federal incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Government and Consumer Services – Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (Ontario Business Central)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under the Business Corporations Act (Ontario)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; no escrow account mandatory. Articles must state authorized share structure with at least one class of shares; shares may be issued for any cash or other consideration not less than fair value.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporation of the Corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Ontario) and the filing of Articles of Incorporation are hereby ratified and approved. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the share subscription of the incorporator(s) is accepted and the shares are allotted and issued as set forth in the subscription records. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the registered office of the Corporation be established at such address in Ontario as approved by the directors, and that legal counsel be engaged to file the required notices and maintain statutory records. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the following persons be and are hereby appointed as the first directors and officers, to hold office in accordance with the by-laws and the Act, with full authority to execute all banking, payroll, and operational contracts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Central / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search using the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system to ensure the proposed corporate name is distinguishable from existing marks. Submit a request through a licensed NUANS service provider and obtain a preliminary search report.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is confusingly similar, select a revised name or submit additional evidence of consent from the prior name holder; refile a new NUANS report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Central / Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation in prescribed Form 1, specifying business name, registered office address, share structure (class, rights, privileges, restrictions), number of directors, and any restrictions on business activities. Executed by the incorporating party and witnessed.
required_dossiers: Notice of registered office (Form 2 optional at filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the filing is deficient, the registry issues a notice of defect; correct the defect and refile within 30 days without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application and Obtain Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Central Online Filing Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation and applicable filing fee online through Ontario Business Central. Upon validation and processing, the Ministry issues a Certificate of Incorporation containing the Ontario incorporation number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected due to incomplete data, use the online correction tool to amend and resubmit; if an objection is raised, file a formal response with supporting clarification to the Branch.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt By-Laws and Appoint Directors and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or adopt written resolutions to approve by-laws, appoint directors, officers, and set the financial year end. Minute the resolution and maintain the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes or written resolution
Consent to act as director/officer forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory filings are missed, obtain unanimous shareholder consent to ratify resolutions and comply with the BCA by filing annual returns or notices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Registered Office and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Ministry of Government and Consumer Services vs. private service agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is within Ontario and maintain statutory records at the registered office or at an authorized records agent. File Form 5 (Initial Return) with the Ministry if required under the BCA and update director/officer information.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the registered office notice is queried, file an updated Form 3 (Change of Registered Office) and pay the requisite fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain CRA Business Number and Payroll Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a federal Business Number (BN) via CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO). Request the applicable program accounts: corporate income tax (RC145), GST/HST (RC148), and payroll deductions (RP145) for the EOR staffing operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, contact CRA's e-services helpdesk or submit a paper application (Form RC1) to the appropriate tax services office; provide corporate identification and supporting incorporation documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development – Employment Agencies and Recruiters Licensing Unit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Employment Agency Licence under the Employment Agencies and Recruiters Act, 2015, SO 2015, c 25, Sch 5

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Administrative office use only; no industrial facility or environmental triggering activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for employer-of-record administrative operations. If installs HVAC systems containing refrigerants, comply with O Reg 517/19 (HFC allowances) and Ontario Environmental Protection Act requirements for ozone-depleting substances. Municipal wastewater and stormwater discharges subject to local sewer use by-laws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection certificate from the local municipal fire department confirming compliance with the Fire Protection and Prevention Act, 1997 and Ontario Fire Code (O Reg 213/07). Also obtain a workplace safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSO 1990, c O.1, including structural load inspection certificate for the leased office premises and proof of occupational first aid and emergency preparedness training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), with registration and compliance services through the Business Registration Online portal and CRA My Business Account; Ontario Ministry of Finance for provincial corporate income tax and Employer Health Tax (EHT) accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Ontario business corporation: (1) incorporate under the Ontario Business Corporations Act or the Canada Business Corporations Act and obtain extra-provincial registration in Ontario if applicable; (2) file Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' or use CRA Business Registration Online to obtain the nine-digit Business Number (BN); (3) request the required CRA program accounts, including corporate income tax (RC), GST/HST (RT), and payroll deductions (RP); (4) register with the Ontario Ministry of Finance for provincial corporate income tax and EHT through the Ontario Business Registry; (5) where an entity has no Canadian establishment, CRA may issue a simplified non-resident GST/HST registration under the Excise Tax Act; a foreign corporation may also use a treaty-based permanent establishment analysis to determine Canadian filing obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' or elective hybrid classification. An incorporated Ontario or federal business corporation is mandatorily taxed at the entity level under Part I of the Income Tax Act. Relevant elections are limited to status-neutral statutory elections, including the closely related corporation election under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act for GST/HST, and voluntary GST/HST registration where the entity is a small supplier. Hybrid mismatch treatment follows statutory rules rather than elective entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Federal Goods and Services Tax and Ontario Harmonized Sales Tax); services are subject to 13% HST in Ontario unless zero-rated or exempt
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold based on worldwide taxable supplies in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; a non-resident carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada must register unless the small-supplier exception applies; voluntary registration is available to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose a mandatory real-time e-invoicing clearance, fiscal stamping, or continuous transaction control regime for GST/HST. Electronic invoices and records are recognized where they meet CRA completeness, legibility, and auditability requirements. CRA mandates electronic filing of GST/HST returns for larger registrants and electronic payroll information returns; no CRA-approved API block-chain stamping or real-time pre-clearance is required in Ontario.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Excise Tax Act and Schedule VI, Part V, a supply of services to a non-resident person is generally zero-rated if the service is not performed in connection with real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada and the supply is not otherwise rendered to an individual present in Canada at the time of performance. For a global EOR and cross-border contractor payroll platform, back-office and administrative services supplied to non-resident clients without a Canadian real-property or goods nexus may qualify for 0% GST/HST; however, the true object of the supply is decisive, and services that constitute the supply of labour or services physically performed in Canada may be taxable at 13% HST. Zero-rating claims must be documented contemporaneously.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable to pure service exports; for any incidental goods, retain a completed CBSA B13A Export Declaration and Transport Canada/forwarder airway bill or bill of lading
Signed international services agreement and purchase order clearly identifying the non-resident recipient and the jurisdictional situs of performance
Proof of non-resident status of the counterparty, such as a completed W-8BEN-E, CRS self-certification, or foreign tax authority certificate
Commercial invoice showing the supply description, amount in CAD, and application of 0% GST/HST with reference to the applicable zero-rating provision
Foreign exchange settlement and inward payment remittance records evidencing receipt of consideration from outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated supplies and claw back input tax credits and refunds if the supporting documentation is incomplete or the true economic substance indicates a taxable Canadian supply. Penalties include the gross-negligence penalty under section 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act of the greater of CAD 250 and 50% of any understated tax or overstated credit, daily compound interest on arrears, and criminal prosecution under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act for willful evasion. Documentary retention for a minimum of six years is mandatory.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); the Government of Canada and the Department of Finance retain policy oversight, with no separate statutory foreign exchange control administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible under a free-floating exchange-rate regime. Canada maintains no exchange controls, no current-account convertibility restrictions, and no capital-control licensing for inward or outward remittances. Profit repatriation in the form of dividends, branch remittances, interest, or management fees may be subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act, and treaty reductions are available, but there is no currency-based barrier or mandatory conversion hurdle. Inbound investments by non-residents are generally open without approval, subject to Investment Canada Act net-benefit review thresholds only for larger acquisitions. Payment instructions and supporting documentation must satisfy anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening requirements, including FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting for transactions of CAD 10,000 or more.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, no designated holding period, and no retention threshold for export receipts. Exporters may lawfully hold foreign currency or Canadian dollars and use proceeds at their discretion. Customs and trade reporting under the Customs Act and Statistics Canada's export reporting regime remains applicable for statistical and administrative purposes, and the tax treatment of export income is calculated in Canadian dollars for Income Tax Act purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account for payroll and settlement; Capital Escrow Account available for segregated inbound capital and intercompany funding.
Operating Account in Canadian or US dollars; Capital Escrow Account accepted for treasury management and non-resident shareholder funding.
Operating Account and cash-management/sweep account; Capital Escrow Account may be opened for regulated payroll or trust-like arrangements.
Operating Account for cross-border disbursements; Capital Escrow Account supported for corporate treasury and statutory payroll reserves.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for contractor payroll, low-value disbursements, and Wise-style cross-border rails; High feasibility is subject to legal constraints. Wise, Payoneer, and similar non-bank payment service providers are not Canadian Schedule I banks and cannot accept deposits in the banking-law sense. They must be registered with FINTRAC as money-services businesses (MSBs) and, if engaged in retail payment activities, comply with the Retail Payment Activities Act and obtain the required authorization or registration from the Bank of Canada. Such platforms may be used as execution channels for international contractor payments, but they should not replace a regulated Canadian banking relationship when statutory employer-of-record obligations, source deductions, CRA remittances, and client escrow requirements demand a deposit-taking institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory obligation requiring every director to appear physically in Ontario or Canada for corporate account opening. Under Canadian AML/KYC rules (PCMLTFA), banks must identify and verify directors, officers, and every ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the entity. Major banks now permit remote onboarding through video identity verification, notarized board resolutions, and electronic verification of corporate status, but at least one signatory or authorized officer with a verifiable Canadian nexus or a registered agent is generally required. A physical branch interview is normally avoidable for a low-risk staffing/EOR entity if the corporate pack is clean and the bank's virtual KYC procedure is followed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership obscured by a chain of offshore holding companies or discretionary trusts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consolidated organizational chart; up-to-date share register; register of directors and officers; certificate of incumbency; UBO declaration for each natural person at or above 25%; FATCA and CRS self-certifications; certified copy of articles/continuance; and official registry search results for every holding entity in the chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth not transparent for a large inbound CAD capital injection or shareholder loan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or interim financial statements; board resolution authorizing the contribution; shareholder capital account statement; funding bank reference letter; executed loan or equity subscription agreement; transaction trail evidencing origin of funds; and a concise source-of-wealth statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media hit on a non-resident director, shareholder, or principal counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full legal name, date of birth, and jurisdiction records for affected persons; detailed sanctions screening output; explanation of any PEP status; independent enhanced due-diligence report; beneficial-ownership chain; supporting legal-identity documents; purpose-of-account narrative; and confirmation of screening status under Canadian Economic Sanctions legislation administered by Global Affairs Canada.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity payroll disbursements to many foreign beneficiaries creating an apparent money-laundering or structuring pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed EOR client services agreement; underlying staffing or contractor agreements; itemized payroll run with beneficiary details; payroll tax filings and CRA remittance confirmations; jurisdiction-specific employment-licence or registration certificates; no-cash payment policy; internal AML compliance program and designated compliance officer; and, where applicable, FINTRAC MSB registration proof.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan funding is routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 cover to the Canadian operating account. The payment should carry a purpose code or narrative clearly identifying the transaction as a capital contribution or shareholder loan (for example, 'EQTI' or 'Capital injection under board resolution — not sales proceeds'), together with the sending bank, beneficiary legal entity, and reference to the underlying corporate resolution. Canada does not require exchange-control approval, but the originating and receiving banks must perform sanctions screening and FINTRAC EFT reporting if the transaction reaches CAD 10,000. Domestic CAD availability is achieved through Payments Canada clearing (ACSS for standard ACH/settlement and LYNX for high-value real-time CAD payments).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border supplier and client payments are executed through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers, normally via a Schedule I bank's global clearing desk. Commercial letters of credit may be used for documentary trade settlements where contractual security or shipment-based assurance is needed. For EOR and staffing operations, Canadian payroll is distributed through local direct deposit using the ACSS; international contractor payments can be routed through Wise or another FINTRAC-registered PSP, or through the bank's cross-border wire product for larger amounts. All outbound instructions must state accurate beneficiary details and payment purpose codes, and must be screened against applicable Canadian sanctions lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forward contracts (1–12 months) with a Schedule I Canadian bank or licensed derivatives dealer
Cross-currency swaps for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/GBP liquidity and balance-sheet hedging
Vanilla foreign-exchange options (call/put) entered into under an ISDA 1998 FX Master Agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with offshore convertibility restrictions, executed as bespoke derivative transactions with a regulated bank and subject to OSFI margin and suitability requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate income tax rate (federal 15% + Ontario 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction reduces combined rate to 12.2% (federal 9% + Ontario 3.2%) on active business income up to CAD 500,000; federal SR&ED investment tax credit of 35% refundable for qualifying CCPCs on eligible expenditures (15% for other corporations); Ontario Innovation Tax Credit of 10% on qualifying innovation expenditures. Non-capital losses may be carried back 3 years and forward 20 years; capital losses carried back 3 years and forward indefinitely.
